READ BY ic 2026-09-02, ON THE CANON SET AT COMMIT 1c80a627. SET: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, usage-rules.md and the 23 canon skills. A JUDGEMENT ON THE RECORD, NOT A MEASUREMENT.

VERDICT: NOT CLEAN, AND THE SET CONTAINS BOTH THE RULE AND ITS VIOLATION -- which is the most useful thing this read found, because the rule is stated correctly, with its reason, in the same repository that breaks it.

THE WORKED POSITIVES FIRST, BECAUSE THEY ARE THE STANDARD THE REST IS JUDGED AGAINST. AGENTS.md declines to reproduce the installed rosters: "Read live rather than reproduced here, because a snapshot of what is installed goes stale the moment anything is installed and nothing regenerates this file to notice", then names the two answering verbs. It does the same for the command reference: "Run intent llm guide before you start ... generated from the tool rather than maintained by hand, so it cannot describe a command that is not there or omit one that is -- which is the failure a written command reference has whenever the tool moves and the document does not." That is this criterion, stated by canon, in canon's own words.

FINDING 1 -- THE PREDICTED FAILURE HAS ALREADY OCCURRED, IN THE SAME SET. usage-rules.md carries a hand-written Skills table of 22 rows. Canon ships 23 skills. THE TABLE OMITS in-content-essentials. So the document AGENTS.md warned would go stale has gone stale, and nothing reported it -- the omission is invisible at the point of use, because a reader consulting a table has no way to know what is not in it. The answering verb exists and is named four lines away in the other document: intent claude skills list.

FINDING 2 -- SAME CLASS, SAME FILE: usage-rules.md also reproduces the subagent roster as a 9-row table, against intent claude subagents list.

FINDING 3 -- usage-rules.md pins a version in its frontmatter example: intent_version: 2.9.1. The tool is 3.0.0. The claim is not load-bearing but it is the class exactly: a value true of one build, in a document nothing re-checks, reading identically after it stopped being true.

FINDING 4 -- THE SHARPEST, BECAUSE THIS ESTATE HAS ALREADY MEASURED WHAT IT COSTS. AGENTS.md pins an exit-code contract in prose: "Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 error." surface/dispatch-table.json records that this exact claim, stated wrongly, would have shipped a permanent silent gate bypass -- the pre-commit hook blocks on 1 and 3 and FAILS OPEN on 2, so a runner built to a wrong exit-code sentence commits unchecked while remaining conformant to the document. Driven here: the runner the shipped gate invokes, bin/intent_critic, exits 3 (CRITIC_REFUSED) at :334 and :347, and AGENTS.md's list has no 3 in it.

AND THE LIMIT OF FINDING 4 IS STATED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED, BECAUSE IT IS THE ROW'S OWN POINT: I could not settle by reading whether v3's intent critic shares that exit set -- there is no critic.rs in intent-cli, the verb resolves at rc=0, and the document does not say which runner its three codes describe. A READER CANNOT TELL FROM THE DOCUMENT WHETHER THE CLAIM IS CURRENT, WHICH IS PRECISELY THE COST THIS CRITERION NAMES.

FINDING 5 -- usage-rules.md maintains roughly sixty lines of command reference by hand, enumerating verbs and flags across nine sections, against a tool that generates exactly this from itself. This is not stale today. It is the mechanism that produced findings 1 to 3, still running.

REACH, DECLARED: usage-rules.md is SEEDED AND NEVER SYNCED (canon.rs:316, "USER-OWNED FILES ARE SEEDED, NEVER SYNCED"), so correcting it fixes THIS repository only and every existing fleet member keeps its copy permanently. AGENTS.md by contrast is generated, so finding 4 is fixed at lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md and reaches everyone on their next agents sync. The two findings have opposite reach and the same appearance, which is worth knowing before either is scheduled.
